newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangsu Expressway debuts at HK$2.80/shr.
newsitem.headline: Jiangsu Expressway debuts at HK$2.80/shr.

text.p: Jiangsu Expressway Co Ltd, the last initial public offering under colonial rule, got off to a poor start on its Hong Kong trading debut on Friday, opening at HK$2.80 per share compared with an issue price of HK$3.11.
Jiangsu Expressway issued 1.222 billion new H-shares, or 25 percent of its enlarged share capital, at HK$3.11 each in a global flotation.
H-shares are shares of China-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.
Of the issued shares, 61 percent were allocated to an international placing, 32 percent to a strategic placing and the remaining seven percent to a public offer.
The Hong Kong public offering was 2.5 times subscribed and the international placing portion was 12 times subscribed.
The strategic placing was made to New World Infrastructure Ltd, COSCO Group and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd.

Jiangsu Expressway, controlled by the communications department in China's Jiangsu province, owns and operates the Jiangsu section of Shanghai-Nanjing (Huning) Expressway connecting Shanghai and Nanjing.
It said net proceeds of about HK$3.65 billion would be used to buy an interest in expressways and participate in other highway development projects, with the balance for working capital.
